title: KronQ: LLM Quantization via Kronecker-Factored Hessian
hook: GPTQ assumes every output channel matters equally. KronQ adds gradient information to challenge that — rescuing 2-bit LLaMA-3-70B from a perplexity blowup down to 7.93.
key_points: GPTQ and GPTAQ build their quantization objective only from input-activation stats, implicitly treating every output channel as equally important.
KronQ adds gradient covariance via a Kronecker-factored Hessian, so quantization loss depends on activation AND gradient statistics.
Bidirectional incoherence processing extends input-side random rotation to the output dimension too, using gradient covariance to cut weight variance.
A new sensitivity metric, from gradient and activation Hessian traces, decides which layers get extra bits in mixed-precision allocation.
At 2-bit weight-only quantization on LLaMA-3-70B, GPTQ/GPTAQ diverge (>2000 WikiText-2 perplexity); KronQ reaches 7.93.
content_html: Post-training quantization methods like GPTQ compress a trained model's weights without retraining, but they define "error" purely from input activations — implicitly assuming every output channel deserves equal protection. Donghyun Lee and colleagues introduce KronQ, which brings gradient covariance into that picture through a Kronecker-factored Hessian approximation, using it both to rotate weights more evenly across input and output dimensions and to decide which layers deserve more bits.
extra_html: The payoff shows up hardest at extreme compression. At 2-bit weight-only quantization on LLaMA-3-70B, the paper reports that GPTQ and GPTAQ diverge or produce degenerate quantizations — perplexity blowing past 2000 on WikiText-2 — while KronQ holds together at 7.93 perplexity. The authors frame this as evidence that ignoring gradient information, as prior second-order PTQ methods do, is a real blind spot once bit-widths get aggressive. Full details are on arXiv.

related.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization
related.hook: Already trained a giant LLM? GPTQ squeezes its weights down to 3–4 bits afterward — no retraining — with surprisingly little quality loss.

related.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Why 'Same Accuracy' Doesn't Mean 'Same Model'
related.hook: Two quantized models can score identically on accuracy while disagreeing on which individual examples they get right — a gap standard benchmarks are structurally blind to.

flashcards.prompt: Why do GPTQ and GPTAQ implicitly treat every output channel as equally important?
flashcards.back_html: They build the quantization objective purely from input-activation statistics, which carries no signal about which output channels matter more.

flashcards.prompt: What does KronQ's gradient covariance get used for?

choices.text: Bidirectional incoherence processing (rotating input AND output dims) plus a sensitivity metric for mixed-precision allocation
Retraining the full model end-to-end before quantizing
Deciding which layers to skip quantizing entirely

flashcards.explanation_html: KronQ uses gradient covariance both to extend random rotation to the output dimension and to derive a per-layer sensitivity score for bit allocation.

flashcards.prompt: At 2-bit weight-only quantization on LLaMA-3-70B, how did KronQ compare to GPTQ and GPTAQ?
flashcards.back_html: GPTQ and GPTAQ collapsed into degenerate quantizations (over 2000 WikiText-2 perplexity), while KronQ stayed usable at 7.93 perplexity.
